**Monday, October 5, 2026 -**_****_

_**Yemen** : Yemen's Saudi-backed government announces operation to retake
Sana'a. Saudi-led coalition deploys 100 warplanes as Yemeni forces launch
offensive. U.S. gives Saudi Arabia over 200 Ansarallah targets but holds off
on direct strikes. Aramco CEO says rebuilding global oil stocks could take two
years._

_**Iran** : U.S. bombers withdrawn from UK's Royal Air Force Fairford base.
Middle East crude exports surpass pre-Iran war levels. Iran's Islamic
Revolutionary Guard Corps orders tanker to turn back in Strait of Hormuz after
string of attacks. Iran summons Norwegian ambassador over Starlink operations.
Iraq to resume direct flights to Iran on Thursday._

_**Palestine:** Israeli attacks kill 15 across Gaza since Saturday. Israeli
forces kill worker, settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West
Bank. Palestinian olive sector loses over $157 million since 2023. Israeli
attacks damage or destroy 82% of Gaza's buildings. Somalia's president says
country won't accept Israeli presence "under any circumstances."_

_**Lebanon:** Israel launches air and artillery attacks across south Lebanon
despite ceasefire._

_**U.S.:** President Donald Trump announces $90 payments to 20 million seniors
from Medicare Improvement Fund, surprising Congress. War Secretary Pete
Hegseth signals some U.S. troops could shift from Europe to Western
Hemisphere. Montana court blocks birthdate requirement on absentee ballots
that led to thousands of rejections. Judge blocks Department of Homeland
Security environmental waivers, slowing border wall construction in Big Bend
region. DHS bought five planes from firm of donor to former Secretary Kristi
Noem at inflated prices in her final hours as secretary. U.S.-Russia Ukraine
talks now include multibillion-dollar Lukoil oil deal tied to Trump allies.
OpenAI head Sam Altman says "world should accept some bad things happening" to
help AI industry. Trump threatens to "double" costs if South Korea doesn't
sign on to Alaska LNG project. Trump posts Sen. Tom Cotton's personal cell
number to pressure him on daylight saving time. California woman arrested for
allegedly spying on Taiwanese president's son for China._

_**International:** U.S. strike on boat in Caribbean kills four. Pro-
government forces seize capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region. Egypt, Eritrea,
Somalia, Sudan leaders issue joint declaration on Ethiopia conflict. Arrested
journalists in Egypt describe torture, forced confessions. Flavio Bolsonaro
outperforms presidential polls, will face current President Luiz Inacio Lula
da Silva in Brazil runoff. Pro-Imran Khan march launches after talks with
Pakistani government collapse. India, Pakistan summon each other's diplomats
over deadly border incident. Mass protests demanding election chief's
resignation enter third day across India. Air strike kills UN aid truck driver
in Sudan's South Kordofan, World Food Program says; Rapid Support Forces
accused of seizing WFP aid trucks. Nationalist party of Serb politician
Milorad Dodik claims victory in Bosnia election despite his ban from office.
Nicaragua withdraws from Central American Parliament. Russia strikes Kyiv
bridge as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz makes unannounced visit. Ukrainian
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready for U.S.-backed trilateral
talks, accuses Russia of sharing jet technology with North Korea. Japan
summons U.S. ambassador after Marine arrested in Okinawa murder. Philippines
accuses Chinese maritime forces of obstructing anti-blast-fishing operation
near Thitu Island._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Yemen

  * **Yemen 's Saudi-backed government announces operation to retake Sana'a:** Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, [announced](https://x.com/presidentrashad/status/2107034488656240969?s=46) Monday the launch of a military and security operation dubbed "Dawn of Yemen," aimed at retaking the capital Sana'a from Ansarallah and restoring control over state institutions.

    * "The Dawn of Yemen operation has begun to restore state institutions, liberate the capital Sana'a, and end the Houthi coup," Al-Alimi said, a day after announcing the start of military operations to "restore the remaining territory of the Republic and extend state authority nationwide."

    * Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti, a member of Ansarallah's political bureau, [dismissed](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2106801618041573617) Al-Alimi's announcement, saying "the war today is between Yemen and Saudi Arabia." He said Saudi aircraft were bombing Yemen while Ansarallah forces were responding "with missiles and drones deep inside Saudi territory," adding that "it is the Saudi regime that controls the mercenary forces, not Rashad al-Alimi."

  * **Saudi-led coalition deploys 100 warplanes as Yemeni forces launch offensive:** The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that 100 fighter jets were taking part in "Operation Dawn of Yemen," providing round-the-clock air support to Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and air cover over the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

    * Coalition spokesperson claimed 324 "high-value" targets had been destroyed since the operation began. The coalition's intervention follows overnight Saudi-backed strikes on Sana'a and the northern province of Saada.

    * On the ground, Saudi-backed forces claimed Monday to have taken large parts of Dhubab district overlooking Bab al-Mandab. They also claimed control of the Dhubab airstrip and key positions around the strait, while Ansarallah-aligned media denied that Saudi-backed forces had advanced. Reuters reported that fighting remained under way in the area.

    * Elsewhere, Saudi-backed forces claimed gains in southern Taiz. The military claimed it had carried out 1,122 attacks across Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and the western coast, killing or otherwise "neutralizing" 1,747 Ansarallah fighters. The figures could not be independently verified.

    * Ansarallah said Sunday it had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Aramco facilities in Riyadh and Khurais, causing major fires. It said the strikes were retaliation for 50 Saudi airstrikes and missiles over the previous 12 hours on Sana'a, al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Hajjah, and Saada.

  * **U.S. gives Saudi Arabia over 200 Ansarallah targets but holds off on direct strikes:** The U.S. military [provided](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/02/saudis-yemen-houthis-bab-al-mandeb-strait) Saudi Arabia with intelligence and targeting data for its operations against Ansarallah in Yemen, including more than 200 targets over the past two weeks, a U.S. official told Axios.

    * Washington has twice rejected recent Saudi requests to directly join the fighting.

    * Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman again asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday for U.S. airstrikes to support a planned Saudi-backed operation in Yemen, but a U.S. official said Washington "is not going to take kinetic action for now."

    * President Donald Trump also held off on ordering strikes against Ansarallah last week after a request from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

    * CENTCOM has raised concerns that direct U.S. involvement in Yemen would divert attention and resources from Iran, according to a U.S. official.

    * U.S. officials said Washington is currently providing Saudi Arabia with support short of direct combat, but direct U.S. military action could still be considered if the Saudi-backed operation runs into difficulties.

  * **Aramco CEO says rebuilding global oil stocks could take two years:** Replenishing global oil inventories while meeting demand could take "up to two years," as disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz continue amid the war with Iran, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said Monday.

    * "The world entered the crisis with oil inventories of around 10 billion barrels" and has since "lost nearly 3 billion barrels" of oil supply, Nasser said, adding that roughly half the crude and refined products normally shipped through Hormuz have been lost. "Less than 6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain, and most of them are practically unavailable."

    * "Emergency reserves may get us through the winter, but they do not solve the supply problem in the long term," Nasser said, warning pressure would continue "until the Strait of Hormuz fully reopens and confidence returns."

    * Aramco is considering additional crude export routes and overseas storage, Nasser said. "If we are asked to provide 12 million barrels per day, we can provide it within days."

# Iran

  * **U.S. bombers withdrawn from RAF Fairford** : The U.S. abruptly [removed](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/04/politics/us-air-force-bombers-removed-fairford-iran) all U.S. long-range bombers deployed to the RAF Fairford airbase in England and returned them to their U.S. home stations over the weekend. The move, which was not explained, comes days after British authorities arrested several individuals over what the officials have claimed was an Iranian plot targeting the base.

    * Fairford has served as a forward operating location for U.S. Global Strike Command and hosted B-1 bombers used in the war against Iran.

  * **Middle East crude exports surpass pre-Iran war levels:** Crude exports from the Middle East exceeded pre-war levels on four of the final seven days of September, reaching 19.5 million to 22.5 million barrels per day (bpd), according to provisional data from ship-tracking firm Kpler reported by Reuters via Al Jazeera. Before the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, exports averaged about 18 million bpd.

    * The seven-day average for crude exports stood at 18.5 million bpd on October 1, while combined flows of crude, refined products, chemicals and other non-gas liquids averaged 22.4 million bpd in the seven days through September 30.

    * IRGC commander Ali Fadavi disputed the scale of traffic Sunday, saying only "three to four million barrels" of oil were moving through the route each day and describing that volume as "negligible" compared with pre-war levels.

    * Kpler's figures include Strait of Hormuz transits, Red Sea flows, terminal exports, and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, but exclude vessels traveling with their tracking transponders switched off.

  * **IRGC orders tanker to turn back in Strait of Hormuz after string of attacks:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps ordered an inbound tanker in the Strait of Hormuz to turn back on Monday, warning that the vessel would otherwise be targeted, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. The tanker complied with the order, which was issued about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman.

    * The incident follows three consecutive days of attacks on tankers in and around the Strait. On Sunday, a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged its engine room. On Saturday, a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side by an unknown projectile four nautical miles east of Oman. On Friday, another tanker was struck during an outbound transit, causing a small fire and blackout before the vessel resumed its journey.

    * No casualties or environmental impacts were reported in any of the three attacks.

  * **Iran summons Norwegian ambassador over Starlink operations:** Iran [summoned](https://en.irna.ir/news/86283399/Iran-lodges-formal-protest-at-Norway-s-inaction-over-illegal) Norway's ambassador in Tehran on Sunday and lodged a formal protest over Oslo's failure to stop unauthorized Starlink operations inside Iran.

    * Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the U.S. and Israel of using Starlink to advance an "interventionist and divisive agenda" in Iran and criticized Norway for taking no effective action despite repeated requests from Tehran.

  * **Iraq to resume direct flights to Iran on Thursday:** Iraqi Airways will [resume](https://ina.iq/ar/local/275359-.html) direct flights to Iran on October 8, Iraq's Transport Ministry announced Monday.

    * The new schedule will include daily flights between Najaf International Airport and Tehran, Mashhad and Isfahan.

    * Iraq halted flights to and from Iran on September 25 in line with U.S. sanctions and subsequently sought exemptions for pilgrimage, medical and educational travel. Reuters reported that the U.S. Treasury exemption for Iraqi Airways runs for one month, with a more permanent arrangement potentially to follow.

# Palestine

  * **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, five Palestinians were killed--three in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 26 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered.

    * The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,243 killed, with 175,232 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,460 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,116, while 836 bodies have been recovered.

    * 181 Palestinians were added to the cumulative death toll after their data was completed and verified, the Ministry noted.

  * **Israeli attacks kill 15 across Gaza since Saturday:** One Palestinian was killed and more than five others were wounded, including two children, on Monday in an Israeli drone [strike](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D9%88%D8%A3%D9%83%D8%AB%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%86-5-%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89) on the southern Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, according to WAFA.

    * Several Palestinians were wounded, including one critically, when an Israeli drone [struck](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A5%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%A7-%D8%AE%D8%B7%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%AE%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86%D8%B3) near the Taiba Towers west of Khan Younis.

    * In northern Gaza, a woman was shot in the head by Israeli naval forces in the Al-Sudaniya area northwest of Gaza City. Another woman was wounded by Israeli quadcopter fire in the Zeitoun neighborhood, southeast of Gaza City.

    * On Saturday, Israeli attacks [killed](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2106599557991653546) nine Palestinians, including four women and a child, across Gaza.

    * An Israeli airstrike on the Al-Asala building in western Gaza City killed five people: two Palestinian Christian women, an elderly woman and her daughter, and one man.

    * Five Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks across the Strip on Sunday.

  * **Israeli forces kill worker, settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces [shot and killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D9%88%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A5%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%87%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%AE%D8%B7%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84) a Palestinian worker and wounded two others, one critically, near the entrance to Bani Naim, southeast of Hebron, on Monday, according to WAFA.

      * Israeli settlers [chased](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8B%D8%A7-%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D8%AD%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%82) ten workers near Khirbet Huwara, east of Yatta, firing into the air and severely beating several of them.

      * Israeli forces also [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%8B-%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%87-%D9%88%D8%AD%D8%B8%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D9%81%D9%8A) a 140-square-meter home sheltering two families in Al-Deirat, east of Yatta, along with a water well, tent and sheep pens.

    * **Jenin:** Three Palestinians were [injured](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-3-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%AE%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%82%D8%B7%D9%81) when settlers attacked olive harvesters in the Khirbet Amriha and Al-Makhal areas, southwest of Jenin. A 42-year-old man suffered a broken leg, another man was injured in his left hand, and an elderly man was beaten and pepper-sprayed, the Palestinian Red Crescent said.

    * **Ramallah:** Settlers [stole](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%88%D9%86) harvested olives and damaged trees in Umm Safa and Al-Mazra'a Al-Gharbiya, northwest of Ramallah, with the latter attack taking place under Israeli military protection. Settlers also attacked olive harvesters in Al-Taybeh, east of Ramallah.

      * Israeli forces separately [raided](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%B5%D8%B1%D8%AD-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AC%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A9) Birzeit University with a military bulldozer, demolished and seized a memorial bearing the names of students killed by Israeli forces, and detained a university security guard.

    * **Nablus:** Settlers [continued stealing olives](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86) from Palestinian farmland in Beita, south of Nablus. In Burqa, northwest of Nablus, settlers attacked farmers harvesting olives in the Bab Al-Jamea area, prevented them from continuing their work and stole a tractor.

      * Six Palestinian families returned to their homes in Tal, southwest of Nablus, after Israeli forces had forced them to leave the houses for more than two months.

  * **Palestinian olive sector loses over $157 million since 2023:** Palestinian farmers [lost](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/5/%D8%A3%D9%83%D8%AB%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%86-157-%D9%85%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AE%D8%B3%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%B5%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86) more than $157 million in olive crops since 2023, while some 286,000 olive trees in the occupied West Bank were damaged between 2023 and the end of September 2026 due to Israeli measures and settler attacks, according to the Palestinian Agriculture Ministry.

    * The ministry said around 100,000 olive trees were damaged in the West Bank in the first nine months of 2026 alone, with crop losses exceeding $67 million. Farmers are currently unable to access roughly 30% of the West Bank's olive-growing land, due to Israeli restrictions, settler attacks, land seizures, and the theft of olive crops.

    * In Gaza, more than 90% of an estimated two million olive trees have been lost since the war began in 2023, alongside extensive destruction of infrastructure supporting the olive sector.

  * **Israeli attacks damage or destroy 82% of Gaza 's buildings:** Around 201,290 buildings in Gaza, or an estimated 82% of all buildings in the Strip, were damaged by Israeli attacks between October 7, 2023 and June 16, 2026, according to the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics.

    * Of those, 134,422 buildings were completely destroyed and another 13,848 severely damaged. Most of Gaza's roughly 2.1 million residents remain displaced and confined to less than 40% of the Strip due to Israeli access restrictions.

  * **Somalia 's president says country won't accept Israeli presence "under any circumstances": **Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud [told](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/3/somalia-wont-accept-israeli-presence-under-any-circumstances-president) Al Jazeera on Sunday that Somalia will not accept an Israeli presence "under any circumstances."

    * In the interview, he alleged that Israel intends to establish a naval base in the port city of Berbera, and to use the city's airport. He called these plans part of a "Greater Israel" project and described Israel as a "destabilizing force" which regularly violates international law.

    * Berbera is within the territory claimed by the self-declared republic of Somaliland, whose statehood Israel became the first to recognize in December 2025. Mogadishu insists Berbera remains part of the Somali Republic.

    * He also told the outlet that the United States remains Somalia's strongest partner against "terrorism."

# Lebanon

  * **Israel launches air and artillery attacks across south Lebanon despite ceasefire:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/566730/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D9%83%D9%81%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A8%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%AA-%D9%88%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%B1-2) strikes on Kfar Tebnit and Wadi Al-Hujair in southern Lebanon on Monday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported, while Israeli forces artillery shelled the outskirts of Hadatha and Bra'shit.

    * Overnight, Israeli shelling also targeted Al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun.

# U.S. News

  * **Trump announces $90 payments to 20 million seniors from Medicare Improvement Fund, surprising Congress:** President Donald Trump announced on Saturday [plans](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/03/trump-announces-plan-send-90-payments-millions-seniors/) to send $90 payments to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees this month, funded by about $2 billion from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which has gone unused for its stated purpose--namely, improving Medicare's hospital and medical insurance programs--since its 2008 creation.

    * The announcement caught congressional offices in both parties by surprise and could unravel unrelated funding talks, a GOP aide told the Washington Post. Lawmakers originally intended to use Improvement Fund monies to help fund several other programs, including the Community Health Center Fund, the National Health Service Corps, the Teaching Health Center Graduate Medical Education program and several special diabetes programs, according to the aide.

  * **Hegseth signals some U.S. troops could shift from Europe to Western Hemisphere** : Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** [told](https://thehill.com/policy/defense/6127801-hegseth-redeploys-troops-western-hemisphere/) reporters on Saturday that some U.S. military capabilities currently in Europe could be redeployed "either back home to the big, beautiful base that we're going to build … or to a different posture in the Western Hemisphere," part of the administration's push for "burden sharing" with the U.S.'s European allies and its increasing focus on military activity in the Western Hemisphere.

    * Hegseth cited expanded partnerships with Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala, and Panama in his remarks on Saturday, crediting "the bold move the president made in Venezuela" in capturing **Nicol as Maduro** with opening "a whole new suite of options economically and militarily." He also reiterated the U.S. is at "war" with cartels, vowing to "posture and base as necessary" to take the fight to what he called "those ISIS and Al Qaeda of our hemisphere."

  * **Montana court blocks birthdate requirement on absentee ballots that led to thousands of rejections** : A Montana state court [ruled](https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/montana-court-blocks-onerous-mail-voting-law-that-caused-thousands-of-rejected-absentee-ballots-last-year/) Friday night that HB 719, a 2025 law requiring absentee voters to include their birthdate on ballot envelopes or have their votes rejected, violates the state constitution, a win for disability advocates who argued the requirement increased the risk of valid ballots being thrown out over technicalities.

    * The law led to nearly 3,000 rejected mail ballots in the November 2025 election in a state where roughly 80 percent of voters cast absentee ballots. State officials failed to produce evidence of voter fraud justifying the law or explain how the birthdate requirement would prevent it, the court noted in its decision, stressing as well "the undisputed fact HB 719 has resulted in thousands of ballots being rejected due to a missing or incorrect birth year."

  * **Judge blocks DHS environmental waivers, slowing border wall construction in Big Bend region** : U.S. District Judge **Kathleen Cardone** [issued](https://www.washingtonsun.com/courts/judge-border-big-bend) a preliminary injunction Friday blocking the Department of Homeland Security from using waivers that exempted border barrier construction from historical and environmental protection laws across more than 500 miles of Texas's Big Bend region, which includes Big Bend Ranch State Park and Big Bend National Park.

    * The order requires DHS to follow those laws while the legal challenge brought by Friends of the Ruidosa Church, river guide **Danny William Miller** and the Center for Biological Diversity proceeds.

    * The ruling follows a separate judge's Thursday denial of a temporary restraining order specific to the national park, where the administration paused work through Sept. 30. DHS has said it is considering reducing the project's scope, for which a $1.7 billion contract was already doled out to construct a "Big Bend border wall." In filings, the administration said it would announce a final decision this week.
